default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-049.title: Volume ignition after a dry-up
E-049.hypothesis: After a stretch where volume runs well below its normal level for the time of day, nobody informed is trading; the first bar with volume several times normal is new information arriving (not churn), and the passive side quoting the quiet market is run over, so follow the ignition bar's direction.

E-050.title: Setup 9.1 failure stop run
E-050.hypothesis: Brazilian retail day traders widely run Larry Williams' setup 9.1 on WIN: buy above the high of the bar that turns the 9 EMA up, stop below that bar's low. When the setup triggers and price then closes back below the turn bar's low, those clustered retail stops are hit together and the trapped longs' exits push the move on; follow the failure (mirror for the sell setup).

E-051.title: Wide outside-bar fade
E-051.hypothesis: A wide bar that takes out both the previous bar's high and low has swept the stops on both sides; when it closes at one extreme, that last sweep was forced stop and chase orders rather than new interest, and with both stop pools spent liquidity providers lean against it; fade the close side.

E-052.title: Developing POC migration
E-052.hypothesis: The developing point of control (the price bin with the most volume today) is where the session has accepted value; when it jumps to a higher bin, buyers have moved the bulk of trade up and responsive sellers failed to hold value lower, so initiative flow continues that way; follow the shift.

E-053.title: Hourly opening-range break
E-053.hypothesis: Execution desks and algos restart schedules at each clock hour, and the first minutes of the hour set a local range many short-term traders mark; the first close beyond it within the hour shows which side the new hour's flow is on, so follow the first break of each hour.

E-054.title: Exact-tick repeated level break
E-054.hypothesis: Several recent bars topping at exactly the same tick show a refreshed resting order (an iceberg) defending it; once a bar closes beyond it the absorber is filled or gone, the stops behind the level fire and the traders who leaned on it cover; follow the break.

E-056.title: Clock-mark bar impulse fade
E-056.hypothesis: At the :00/:15/:30 marks scheduled orders (time-sliced algos, timed stops, alerts) hit the book together, so a mark bar that is large for its minute and closes decisively is a mechanical burst, not new information; once it is done liquidity returns and price reverts; fade the mark bar.

E-057.title: Decelerating run reversal
E-057.hypothesis: A run of same-direction bars whose bodies shrink bar after bar shows each push finding fewer aggressive takers; when the next bar closes against the run, the late chasers of the weakest push are under water and the momentum side has stopped paying up; fade the run.

E-058.title: ADX trend-start follow
E-058.hypothesis: Wilder's ADX is on most retail platforms and a cross above its threshold is a common 'trend has started' trigger; when it crosses, directional movement has become one-sided and DI-based trend followers join in the leading DI's direction, extending the move; follow the cross.
